See also: chůva

Macanese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Portuguese chuva.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈt͡ʃu.va/

Noun

[edit]

chuva

  1. rain
    chuva filo-filo ― a drizzle (literally, “sons rain”)
    chuva fino-fino ― light rain (literally, “very thin rain”)
    chuva pedra ― hail (literally, “(hail)stone rain”)
    Não é de costume ter chuva em outubro
    It's not usual to have rain in October

Derived terms

[edit]
  • cai chuva

References

[edit]
  • https://www.macaneselibrary.org/pub/english/uipatua.htm#c

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
chuva
Wikipedia pt

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • chuiva, chúvia, choiva (dialectal)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese chuvia, from Latin pluvia. Compare Galician choiva, Spanish lluvia.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʃu.vɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʃu.vɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʃu.va/
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈʃu.vɐ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈʃu.vɐ/
    • (Northern Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈt͡ʃu.bɐ/ [ˈt͡ʃu.βɐ]

  • Audio (Portugal):(file)
  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -uvɐ
  • Hyphenation: chu‧va

Noun

[edit]

chuva f (plural chuvas)

  1. rain
    • 1980, “A Chuva Cai”, performed by Beth Carvalho:
      A chuva cai lá fora / Você vai se molhar / Já lhe pedi, não vai embora / Espere o tempo melhorar / Até a própria natureza, / Está pedindo pra você ficar
      The rain is falling out there / You're gonna get wet / I already asked, don't go outside / Wait for the weather to get better / Even nature itself / Is asking you to stay
